reviewer: Editorial source review assisted by Codex
scope: Five existing species profiles: Geonosian, Mon Calamari, Sullustan, Zabrak and Twi’lek. All forty inherited fields assessed; nine verified/corrected and 31 unestablished raw values retained. Fourteen new scoped facts and selected work/member/homeworld links. No new identities, episodes, release dates, editions or credits.

summary.text: The winged Geonosians inhabit hive colonies on Geonosis. Their factories arm the Separatists during the Clone Wars, and their engineers contribute to the first Death Star. In Rebels, Klik-Klak guards a queen egg after the Empire devastates his people.

summary.text: Zabrak are recognizable by the horns on their heads. Eeth Koth is identified as an Iridonian Zabrak, while Maul comes from Dathomir. The Nightbrothers are a Dathomirian community of Zabrak warriors, with a culture distinct from the species as a whole.

evidence.locator: Main profile / horned species and two named examples
Eeth Koth section / Iridonian Zabrak and Iridonia
Main profile / Dathomirian male Zabrak warrior community
Official current species identity and selected screen-work context
evidence.note: Creative-era label describes selected screen contexts; it does not validate inherited statistics.

records.scope: First scoped review of this inherited species identity: all eight legacy fields assessed, original short description, selected morphology/culture and named work/member/homeworld connections. Not a complete biological, demographic or screen-appearance inventory.
limitations: The official species page names Dathomir as a location; it does not name it as the origin of every Zabrak. The Council article establishes Iridonia as Eeth Koth’s homeworld, not a universal species homeworld. The inherited species-to-Iridonia homeworld row therefore remains legacy.

Nightbrothers are a historical male warrior community on Dathomir, not a synonym for all Zabrak. Their sex, governance, hostility or combat skill is not generalized to the entire species; the separate ship The Nightbrother is not a biological group.
Maul’s own profile labels him both Dathomirian and Zabrak. These labels are retained in context without inventing an exhaustive subspecies taxonomy or merging the existing Dathomirian species record.

Eeth Koth’s 1.87 m and Maul’s nominal 1.84 m do not establish the inherited 180 cm species mean. No mammalian class, formal sentience designation, language, lifespan or complete eye/hair/skin palette is established by the selected sources.

Additional Solo, Rebels and Maul – Shadow Lord links represent the explicitly identified Zabrak Maul in his own named work list; they do not certify a whole-population scene. His existing biography and episode representation distinctions remain intact.

summary.text: Twi’leks are humanoids from Ryloth with varied skin colours and paired head-tails called lekku. They communicate in Twi’leki and can also use lekku gestures. Many families preserve their history in a Kalikori, adding to it across generations.

limitations: The inherited mammals label is replaced with the explicitly stated humanoid form; sentient is explicit in the Story Group article. Tall and thin does not establish a 200 cm species mean, and a rainbow of colours does not certify the inherited exhaustive seven-colour list.

Twi’leki is explicitly named in the species-culture article and Ryloth introduction. Lekku gestures complement spoken language; they do not establish a quantified telepathic ability or a sole language for every individual.

Kalikori traditions are described as common family practice, not mandatory for every Twi’lek. The original summary avoids copying the Databank’s aesthetic judgments or reducing the species to servitude.

The Mandalorian link is supported by the article’s explicit Xi’an screen example; it does not add Xi’an as a newly reviewed profile. Hera, Cham, Bib and Aayla membership links do not review their personal measurements or appearances. The old Ayla Secura title/slug are retained despite the official Aayla spelling.
